198a2debb377abb7.text: What do you think will roll out of the box?

4083d0558c7e1783.text: In the quiet workshop, a little green light blinked on. Beep.

be1613b3bddb0dd6.text: On Tuesday he found two spinning blue gears. Whir, whir!

e2c9b2f4d14a0579.text: On Monday he found one shiny red battery. Click! But his engine was still hungry.

89954d66fed20eaf.text: On Wednesday he found three bouncy yellow springs. Boing, boing, boing!

cc317e903c1fe822.text: What did the robot find on Tuesday?

94add0e38c7aabe3.text: On Thursday he found four twisting green bolts. Squeak, squeak, squeak, squeak!

2f8609eabaa62ca3.text: On Friday he found five glowing purple wires. Zap, zap, zap, zap, zap!

be0ff838e9fd8c95.text: He is still hungry. What might he do on Saturday?

a58e7fc94e87f59a.text: On Saturday he attached one magnet, two sirens, three tracks, four antennas, and five bells.

89e2a6cf6c547123.text: Bzzzt! He was too heavy, too loud, and too bright. He had a system overload.

4f923e7fc3d3ddff.text: On Sunday he unhooked the extra parts and took a long drink from one golden oil can.

2c9138f7c8d37071.text: He rolled into his charging pod for three quiet days, and his new parts began to fuse.

4416361facb78434.text: Then he powered on and pushed the doors open. Swoosh!

969fab4b5d5c8889.text: He was not a clunky grey robot any more. He was a zooming, rainbow hover-bot.

34b5c1afe615a423.text: What came first — the oil can, the red battery, or the hover-bot?

0f5cd6a253ebfc39.text: How do you think he felt when he flew?

d8e1e1c51d498887.text: Look at the pictures. Tell the story in the right order.

96410621fe93aef3.text: He was not a hungry little robot any more. He had learned when enough was enough.

f71c02a277fa8908.text: The hover-bot zoomed away, light, and glad.

45f8be71b60d5f13.text: Noah sat at the table. He made a blue snail out of plasticine.

a627a252648b62cd.text: His baby sister crawled over. She grabbed his blue plasticine!

2bc944c08605e1bf.text: How do you think Noah feels?

b76d9f6bf8215b37.text: Noah felt hot and cross. He wanted to push her away.

229f84f9505a5251.text: But Noah kept his hands to himself. Pushing can hurt a baby.

3baab9e50834f614.text: Why should Noah not push his baby sister?

afb056d4bbba9006.text: He put a hand on his tummy. He took one slow, deep breath.

4c7eae87ad2ea455.text: Then another. His body felt calm again.

580ce1e0d9b57d30.text: What did Noah do to feel calm?

1d120995ef7d4717.text: What do you think Mama will do?

1f024eb3168f738b.text: Noah used his words. "Mama, she took my plasticine. Can you help?"

20a1818745e6719f.text: Mama gave the baby a soft rattle. Plasticine is not safe for babies.

c6d6f5c780f2c6f2.text: Noah got his blue plasticine back. He smiled.

abfb97bd318141aa.text: What came first — the deep breath, or asking Mama?

5340a9e38e08ee40.text: How do you think Noah felt at the end?

d5207d93ca39b640.text: Noah made his snail. His sister shook her rattle. They played side by side.

9d548e4fb2164ca1.text: When Noah feels cross, he keeps gentle hands, takes a breath, and uses his words.

d51c593c8738c2c2.text: On Sunday morning, a tiny egg sat on a quiet leaf.

be78b6ce7e19d9f1.text: What do you think will hatch from the egg?

0478b87da348e832.text: On Monday the egg cracked. Out came a snail no bigger than a pea.

f8e7f1697dfb05d4.text: He was hungry. On Monday he ate one sweet strawberry.

72ac304b996c1b41.text: On Tuesday he ate two plump blueberries.

6fdda90b7f48e13e.text: On Wednesday he ate three soft mushrooms.

5cfacd9a8cc460c2.text: What did the snail eat on Tuesday?

3c454d85b4493fce.text: On Thursday he ate four round peas.

c8eee3313541027d.text: On Friday he ate five ripe raspberries.

8359d0b57e06c1d2.text: On Saturday he ate an enormous feast: a leaf, a plum, a bean, and a whole cucumber.

b5411383b895a0bf.text: That night his tummy ached. He had eaten far too much.

4fcaabfa7632abeb.text: On Sunday he rested on a cool stone and sipped a drop of dew.

15299df50447aa6f.text: After a long rest he felt better. His shell had grown into a beautiful spiral.

bd89c15583c4b017.text: What came first — the feast, the egg, or the spiral shell?

110b137806b56e40.text: How do you think the snail felt when his shell grew?

e4c43e8ab7f48481.text: He was not a tiny snail any more. He had learned to listen to his tummy.

bcfee49b8d367288.text: The snail slid slowly home, full, and glad.

58578570eb195033.text: It was bedtime. The room was dark and quiet.

944a01a39824681d.text: Noah saw a big shape on the wall. His tummy felt wobbly.

907fca90f3241e9b.text: What do you think the big shape really is?

198b6641d8992c92.text: Noah did not hide. He called, "Mama, can you come?"

2345703087df130a.text: Mama turned on a little nightlight. The shape was only his coat on the chair!

972c337dee64cdeb.text: "It is just a shadow," said Mama. Noah took a slow breath.

71ad3758d04a0e0e.text: Why did the nightlight help Noah?

4b0bffda484706a6.text: Noah hugged his teddy. The nightlight glowed softly. He fell asleep.

1b571a0b9c2bde9f.text: How did Noah feel at the end?

c33b2248bd93ba9d.text: When Noah feels scared, he calls for help and takes a slow breath.

7d7ee57d9427ecb2.text: Noah had a bowl of soft banana slices. Yum!

f3d10f25a882c2be.text: Baby sister sat in her high chair. She reached for the bowl.

e58857d9b5c0c0f6.text: Baby sister wants some banana. What could Noah do?

a5bc8b69ab10e55b.text: Noah gave her one slice. Then another. He shared.

e5dbd2575e12d104.text: Noah and his sister ate their snack together.

731b4cd1c530919c.text: Why did Noah still have a snack after sharing?

36bfe24c081d7322.text: Look where the car is going. What do you think will happen?

f84ec6cd34ac90c3.text: Baby sister made a tower of soft blocks. Noah zoomed his car across the rug.

f2b28587bde802c9.text: Crash! The car hit the tower. The blocks fell down.

add373be16f5a5f1.text: Baby sister cried. Noah did not mean to do it. It was an accident.

f1cdcf733cafc46b.text: Noah knelt down. He patted her back gently. "I am sorry," he said.

df072335f0bcd7b4.text: What did Noah say to his sister?

dad5107f69693e00.text: Then Noah helped her build the tower again.

03ef16672e263a96.text: Why did Noah say sorry, if it was an accident?

38c53d1ee6b60df3.text: What came first — saying sorry, or building again?

c69d4e15acbcc89f.text: The new tower was even taller. Baby sister clapped.

015734c738eed0dd.text: Even after an accident, Noah says sorry and helps fix it.

c570664943752287.text: Blocks, cars, and crayons were all over the rug. What a mess!

c44186d6b5cf15a0.text: Noah did not want to tidy. It looked like too much.

8f0bae28545182e0.text: How could Noah make the big job feel smaller?

18065559955c96fa.text: So Noah started small. First, just the blocks. Clunk, clunk, into the basket.

be8a663383e0cea0.text: What did Noah put away first?

db7c8a65d4b704bd.text: Baby sister wanted to help. She dropped in a soft toy. Plop!

b9bc7eb85b98dc6b.text: Soon the rug was clean. Noah felt proud.

0b4668b03c8e32f1.text: Why did starting with just the blocks help?

22b14588ee9761ef.text: What came first — the blocks, or sister's soft toy?

f2786fc607270819.text: A big job is easy when you do one small part at a time.

0c13ccdc3360aa6f.text: Noah ran to the slide. A girl in a red coat was there first.

ab6a5fb3378d9493.text: Noah wants to slide now. What do you think he will do?

9351e72a6a9c3045.text: Noah wanted to go first. But it was her turn.

9cd7f214279cf6fd.text: What did Noah do while he waited?

21b6fa17ad8f19a6.text: So Noah waited. He counted on his fingers. One, two, three, four, five.

b4990debf83f6ca3.text: Whoosh! The girl slid down. Now it was Noah's turn.

1049d9e216f47cf5.text: Noah climbed up and slid down. Whee!

754668970be7d0a8.text: Why did Noah have to wait?

c4b26290ed1cf339.text: What came first — counting, or sliding?

c8a1ba797df97ffe.text: How do you think the girl felt when Noah waited?

90c20eb59e1d5d1a.text: The girl smiled at Noah. Waiting made a new friend.

ff8bfd4c9bb86519.text: When it is not his turn yet, Noah waits and counts.

e0c6899758134344.text: A little paper boat sat on a round globe.

4088e323f2e34249.text: The boat is ready to sail. Which land do you think he will see first?

c05d896085d38046.text: First he sailed to Africa. The land was wide and warm.

528a36d045613fd4.text: Next he sailed to Antarctica. The land was white and still.

1306540882553231.text: Which land was white and still?

b11804c468a173d3.text: Then he sailed to Asia. The land was vast, with high mountains.

1e59a0ae4b8ccb6e.text: He sailed to Australia. A red rock rose in a quiet desert.

ba73402171e1f700.text: He sailed to Europe. Green fields met a grey sea.

fa82151a364d9508.text: He sailed to North America. Tall trees stood by a cool lake.

e17dfd656329b90a.text: He sailed to South America. A long river ran through a green forest.

7966e629408e8605.text: He has seen all seven lands. What might he do now?

56661016080e1438.text: Why did the little boat stop sailing?

1a29094464045dda.text: What came first — Antarctica, the globe, or Australia?

ceb61ee48fc15fdb.text: How do you think he felt when the trip was done?

ca2996a0f510ea7e.text: He was not lost. He had learned the seven quiet lands.

da6c9b8ab33c2177.text: The little boat folded his sail and rested.

47714796a69a52c6.text: Out rolled a tiny grey robot. His battery blinked low, and he was hungry for parts.

ddf4eaaa938a1cd6.text: The Little Rocket and the Nine Planets.

4394387327d3d5bf.text: The rocket wants to visit every planet. Which one do you think is closest to the Sun?

f6978e4ef398a39a.text: First he flew to Mercury. It was small, grey, and very close to the Sun.

f866e5c0c943a219.text: Next he flew to Venus. Thick yellow clouds wrapped it up.

2da5456dd6b4ef56.text: Then he flew past Earth. Blue sea, green land. That is our home.

100c183dd0ae42b7.text: He flew to Mars. The ground was red and dusty.

af2d5257b7834261.text: He flew to Jupiter. It was huge, the biggest planet of all.

1d14f209106aafe0.text: He flew to Saturn. Wide, flat rings went all the way around it.

7308606dd86e3aed.text: Which planet had wide rings around it?

51b0ad305f70879f.text: He flew to Uranus. It was pale blue, and it spun on its side.

e4e4be7760174423.text: He flew to Neptune. It was deep blue, cold, and far away.

e7a60874444e10ea.text: Last, he flew to little Pluto. It is a dwarf planet, tiny and icy.

4dad6a0b7950a586.text: He has seen all nine. What might he do now?

3252eb495a4fd45c.text: He had visited eight planets and one dwarf planet.

d2d71460aeb63660.text: What came first — Mars, Mercury, or Saturn?

0119b10cdc2a0ebf.text: How do you think he felt so far from home?

6ecd1a2b7a01d42c.text: Look at the pictures. Tell the trip in the right order.

68ec94f23b824367.text: The little rocket flew back to the warm Sun and rested.

5b4a06b0d758622f.text: A little paper rocket floated near the big, warm Sun.

bf4e4826a718f398.text: The Little Digger Builds a Park.

79eb433540b83974.text: Today the big machines would build a park.

0faa3f67aeaff9ba.text: A little yellow digger looked at an empty, sandy lot.

ddc7d0ca344ad9c5.text: Which machine pushed the sand flat?

d78bb0756abcdaf5.text: First the little digger dug a hole. Scoop, lift, drop.

6d648eb0786b658f.text: Then the bulldozer pushed the sand. Its wide blade made it smooth and flat.

3685818c9286f235.text: The dump truck came. It tipped up and poured out grey gravel.

6e17de79e24c8857.text: The cement mixer turned and turned. Then it poured smooth, wet cement.

f89fa1b9904a4836.text: The tall crane lifted a little play house. Slowly, gently, down it came.

978e90d9f76c9dcb.text: The path is still soft and bumpy. Which machine could make it flat?

31a69a1554769c56.text: The road roller rolled the path. Roll, roll, roll, until it was smooth.

2e23ca3a008cadfb.text: Why did the crane lift the play house slowly?

26dc2a78bf3a89a4.text: The work was done. There was a path, a slide, and a little play house.

a6d7613f9a38f41b.text: What came first — the crane, the digging, or the road roller?

1705c5f36a9a7709.text: How do you think the little digger felt when the park was done?

08c1d1e44118dd8b.text: Each machine did its own job. Together, they built a park.

5e3ab2e5022afe53.text: The land is bumpy and bare. What do you think the machines will do first?

31a03f4cb0106230.text: The little digger parked by the slide and rested.

ca7ace53d89e88a8.text: On Monday she crawled to one soft ball. Roll, roll.

9ddcefb0462155b5.text: Nadine is Noah's baby sister. She could not walk yet. She could only crawl.

972e7bd9bd26eddd.text: Nadine loves to crawl. Where do you think she will go this week?

abf4dab0a840f139.text: What did Nadine find in the bath?

d54dbe73982898cf.text: On Tuesday she crawled to two wooden blocks. Bang, bang.

0be18497aedbf552.text: On Wednesday she found three yellow ducks in the bath. Splash, splash, splash.

b2ab6b953958a783.text: On Thursday she crawled to four picture books. Pat, pat, pat, pat.

091c8841456f04e8.text: On Friday she found five shiny pots. Clang, clang, clang, clang, clang!

3a9d6910e8cb17d6.text: Each day she went to more things. What might happen on Saturday?

438faee2d088ab50.text: How do you think Nadine felt after crawling everywhere?

7af67d0011f5cd1f.text: On Saturday she crawled everywhere. Under the table, behind the sofa, and round and round the rug.

dce8484885f4bfa7.text: On Sunday Mama wrapped her in a soft blanket. Nadine had a long, long nap.

85a5c5ac4d72e6bc.text: What came first — the long nap, the ball, or the pots?

ede4c48655ea57ed.text: When she woke up, Nadine stood up. One step, two steps, three. She walked to Noah!

32ffc144afe45d42.text: How do you think Noah felt when Nadine walked to him?

fb7070e2fbc56f25.text: Nadine was not a crawling baby any more. She was a walking girl.

c89518d0e7a54aa7.text: On Sunday night, Noah went to bed with an empty tummy.

e670dca2519fe182.text: When Noah wakes up, how do you think his tummy will feel?

7a9327a3363e1f07.text: On Monday he woke up hungry. He ate one yellow banana.

7070644da42ea54b.text: On Tuesday he ate two crunchy carrots.

79e767406fc735c1.text: On Wednesday he ate three slices of juicy watermelon.

553bacd025c55ebc.text: What did Noah eat on Tuesday?

004e5daeb2450e04.text: On Thursday he ate four red strawberries.

1464fe48b84e35c3.text: On Saturday there is a party. What might Noah eat there?

ab2cd3c2f72171ec.text: On Friday he ate five little tomatoes. But he was still hungry.

cf363f99d2d4fb3c.text: On Saturday he ate cake, ice cream, sweets, chips, a cookie, and a big pink cupcake!

8a6790c2050de6cf.text: That night, Noah had a tummy ache. Ouch.

a3d05bbce28f24e8.text: On Sunday he ate a warm bowl of soup with green peas. His tummy felt calm again.

d8cc11a938ce55b8.text: Mama measured him on the wall. Noah had grown taller!

6f3176270f8fcb2b.text: How do you think Noah felt when he saw how tall he was?

7398145e62998b69.text: Noah was not a little boy any more. He was a big, strong brother.

31124d2fe19efa8e.text: What came first — the soup, the banana, or the party?

f608671e522a04d3.text: Tectonic plates pulled apart. A crack opened. Pressure built.

1fd9de00ee97ba77.text: Deep under the ocean, Blippi, Terrence, and Biscuit Monster watched the seabed.

1c52ff6513e75922.text: Super-hot liquid rock escaped the mantle. Magma rose. It burst into the freezing ocean.

c5e3c6c8421e6726.text: What sound did the water make when it met the hot rock?

e2a02154e1ae6b9c.text: Eruption after eruption, the underwater mountain grew taller. Thousands of years.

0a66e6b2f779f5bd.text: Sssss! Cold water met molten rock. Giant black pillow basalt formed under the sea.

478e0311aed7ac5b.text: The mountain keeps growing. What might happen when it reaches the waves?

e613b03221340ee0.text: The rock broke through the waves. Clouds of steam shot into the sky. Terrence covered his ears.

75a879d9adf7c382.text: A crack is open in the seabed. What do you think will come out?

5d9e6290c276993b.text: Why did the lava turn hard?

d6d37e8dbd318439.text: The volcanic soil cooled. Green seeds arrived on the wind. An island was born.

7d790bbf9a560c8c.text: Biscuit Monster sniffed a leaf. Blippi said, From a crack in the floor to a home for plants.

32fefea81a170b4d.text: What came first — the green seeds, the crack, or the steam in the sky?

ae8acff1950f0270.text: How do you think they felt when the green seeds grew?

4d753b7f449e01e2.text: Look at the pictures. Tell how the island was built.

9ea91192243516fd.text: Crack. Rise. Steam. Pile. Breach. Cool. Life. That is how lava builds an island.

21b9addcdbeb2fcb.text: Blippi, Terrence, and Biscuit Monster floated in dark space. A cold cloud of gas hung still.

6cbc7d9792b4ff5c.text: Hydrogen dust pulled together. Gravity got stronger and stronger.

b187eb1b94709514.text: The cloud is squeezing tight. What do you think it will become?

3a742c9007bbdb18.text: The gas balled up. The middle got hot. Ten thousand degrees. One hundred thousand degrees!

d767527c677a5afe.text: Ignition! A baby star turned on its light. Terrence clapped.

47cb1dea2292fa75.text: The yellow star burned clean fuel for a very long time. It pushed heat out. Gravity pulled in.

4a0d5dff572658f8.text: Push out. Pull in. Perfect balance. Blippi called it a happy star.

3f9b763a47233290.text: What colour was the star when it was in balance?

3d17741105c8c6f2.text: The hydrogen fuel ran low. The middle shrank. The outside swelled huge and red.

54a00b198f15a039.text: The red giant swallowed the nearest planets. Biscuit Monster hid behind Terrence.

c640c3d35cd3e6cc.text: The fuel is almost gone. What might happen next?

9a337642c7471d31.text: Core collapse! BOOM. The star blasted heavy metals into the galaxy.

179d1db5719fc5d1.text: All that remained was a tiny, dense neutron core, spinning in the dark.

801db73a2a8ce7a1.text: How do you think Terrence felt at the end?

5c1d6bfe58b8aef7.text: What came first — the yellow star, the cloud, or the boom?

07357f6af73a9293.text: Look at the pictures. Tell the life of the star in the right order.

f2272ac109636062.text: Blippi whispered, Five steps. Cloud, baby star, yellow star, red giant, boom.

45c4f193a6f48011.text: Blippi, Terrence, and Biscuit Monster lined up the planets by size. Smallest to biggest.

99be10526a071813.text: Which planet do you think is the smallest?

145ebef70a75ac03.text: Category A. The Rocky Scouts. Small and solid.

be1b9fbe9026270e.text: Mercury. Four thousand eight hundred seventy-nine kilometers across. A pocket-sized rock. Zero air.

edcf05fca56de5fb.text: Mars. Six thousand seven hundred seventy-nine kilometers. Red dust. Two tiny moons.

b39ed0434b6cdf0b.text: Venus. Twelve thousand one hundred four kilometers. Heavy yellow clouds. A runaway hot oven.

9196e87a5761bc23.text: Which rocky planet has zero air?

e65fe199b1c04834.text: Earth. Twelve thousand seven hundred forty-two kilometers. Liquid water. Nitrogen air. Life confirmed.

6f889938108f159c.text: Category B. The Ice Giants. Frozen gas and water.

fbd1bf77548eb762.text: Neptune. Forty-nine thousand two hundred forty-four kilometers. Methane blue. Super-fast wind storms.

25b2d9a27d5aafdc.text: Why are Neptune and Uranus called ice giants?

8ed047909aeb544c.text: Uranus. Fifty thousand seven hundred twenty-four kilometers. A cyan ice ball. Tilted on its side.

e7d8a2421df7ebd9.text: Category C. The Gas Titans. Massive and made of spinning gas.

09bae6ecee3d5f83.text: Saturn. One hundred sixteen thousand four hundred sixty kilometers. Light hydrogen. Wide ice rings.

dc4efaeed79d9cd8.text: Jupiter. One hundred thirty-nine thousand eight hundred twenty kilometers. The king. Ninety-five moons. A giant red storm.

14130f64eab99d85.text: What is smallest to biggest — Jupiter, Mercury, or Earth?

305bb2d5d5629b80.text: How do you think Biscuit Monster felt next to giant Jupiter?

a33519622ae76a38.text: Look at the pictures. Sort them from smallest to biggest.

c4f1bb821c554e6e.text: Terrence tapped the list. Rocky scouts. Ice giants. Gas titans. Size is a kind of map.

7df8452b09d760d8.text: Blippi held a clay Earth. Terrence said, Let us slice it. Biscuit Monster licked his lips. Not for eating!

05f9b8f147104838.text: Layer zero. The crust. We stand on cold, hard rock.

5806aa720242e6c2.text: Continents of granite. Oceans of deep blue water. The crust is thin, like the skin of an apple.

fbde1cc99f838cdf.text: If we drill down under the crust, what do you think we will find?

9d59d480b73a619f.text: Layer one. The upper mantle. Drill down. The rocks turn red-hot.

8ae08371ab3281f6.text: What is the thin outer layer called?

14db35a22894f353.text: Giant plates slide on soft, flowing stone. This is where magma sleeps.

05a756009c13a487.text: Layer two. The lower mantle. Crushing pressure! The rock cannot melt. Gravity squeezes it tight.

f8011cc3d18679d3.text: Layer three. The outer core. A swirling sea of liquid iron and nickel.

673f2deea132cf40.text: It flows and churns. This moving metal builds Earth's magnetic shield. It blocks solar storms.

a4e07218a53894dc.text: Why does Earth need a magnetic shield?

3cae7993bb899935.text: Layer four. The inner core. Six thousand degrees. As hot as the surface of the Sun!

9a9b1ed2e0ff1641.text: A solid ball of white-hot iron, locked under billions of tons of weight. The heart of the world.

e5a1f7c939cc7f81.text: The black lava cooled into hard basalt. Waves smashed against the new cliffs.

11ff712640666b3b.text: Terrence counted. Crust. Mantle. Outer core. Inner core. Four layers under our feet.

43dedd6b4425c1a3.text: How do you think Biscuit Monster felt at the hot heart?

3892cab7d2f14284.text: Look at the pictures. Tell the layers from the outside in.

d4a1ed877c852a07.text: What comes first if you start on the outside — the inner core, the crust, or the outer core?

b09919d50badf1d7.text: Blippi held up dark glasses. Never look at the Sun with bare eyes. Special glasses keep us safe.

db3d75067fd89783.text: Noah, baby sister Nadine, SpongeBob, Squidward, and Blippi sat on a quiet hill. The Sun was round and bright.

24847fe77beeb748.text: The Moon slid in. A little bite of the Sun was gone. SpongeBob whispered, Wow.

2545e88f7aa9ad65.text: Why did they wear special glasses?

6f3cd67777adaaa8.text: More and more of the Sun was covered. The hill went grey. Squidward said, It is getting dim.

24fc4298b7cef385.text: The Moon covered the Sun. A white ring shone around the black circle. That ring is the corona.

43e64e51b649d3a9.text: Day felt like night. Nadine held Noah's hand. Nobody looked up without the glasses.

6211d6988c272d58.text: The Moon is still moving. What do you think will happen next?

9737af3aaa3ad544.text: A bead of gold popped out. The Sun was coming back. Blippi cheered.

8c9eb3acf144ef85.text: Light poured over the hill. Birds called. Squidward took off his glasses and blinked.

d70fd18f939f8b40.text: Why did the hill go grey?

1ffb4953c2dafdf2.text: How do you think Noah felt when Nadine held his hand?

675c6f18bf5d88f0.text: What came first — the white ring, the bright Sun, or the grey hill?

f642791f28020f90.text: Look at the pictures. Tell the eclipse in the right order.

aa516ba5a47786fc.text: The Moon moved on. The Sun was round and bright again. Nadine clapped. The eclipse was done.

46ba7bf51f8cde6e.text: Something is going to slide in front of the Sun. What do you think it is?
